_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'Physics Syllabus, Grade 10-12' (2013, published by CDC) — Grade 10, Topics 10.1-10.2. Topic, sub-topic and Specific Outcome statements only; the 'Content' (Knowledge/Skills/Values) columns are omitted, consistent with the approach used for the other 2013 OBC subjects in this app. This document's outcome numbering is reliable and matches its sub-topic structure. Grade 10 genuinely covers only two Topics — Measurements and Mechanics — confirmed by the Grade's own general-outcomes statement at the start of the syllabus, which names only these two areas; Mechanics (10.2) is simply very large, with seven sub-topics covering vectors, linear motion, forces, moments, work/energy/power, simple machines and pressure. Physics topic numbers continue sequentially across grades in this syllabus (Grade 10 ends at Topic 10.2, Grade 11 begins at Topic 11.3) rather than each grade restarting its own topic count — this is a distinctive, deliberate numbering choice by this syllabus, not an error. The syllabus organizes content by Grade only, not by Term, so all of Grade 10 is modeled as a single term here. STRUCTURAL TERM SPLIT (2026-08-31, not sourced): this file's topics were previously modeled as a single undivided 'Year' block (no real per-topic term/week data exists for this subject/grade). At the user's own explicit request and choice among alternatives offered, the SAME real topics/sub-topics above have now been divided into three roughly-equal-by-content-volume groups, in their original curriculum order, labelled 'Term 1'/'Term 2'/'Term 3' purely so the app can generate and share one term at a time. This division is NOT sourced from any real scheme of work - it is an organizational split only. No topic, sub-topic, competency, or objective was added, removed, or altered; only the grouping changed. With only 2 real top-level topics here, the split was done at sub-topic granularity instead of topic granularity (otherwise a 3-way split isn't possible) - Topic '10.1 Measurements' and '10.2 Mechanics' each legitimately reappear across more than one term as a result, carrying only the sub-topics assigned to that term, the same way this app already represents a real topic whose teaching genuinely spans a term boundary. Each sub-topic still has no real week_number of its own, so within a term the app's existing calendar-pacing engine spreads them algorithmically across that term's real teaching weeks, exactly as it already did for the whole undivided Year block.

subject.name: Physics
subject.description: Senior Secondary Physics syllabus, Grade 10-12 (Curriculum Development Centre, 2013).

competencies.description: Distinguish between basic and derived quantities
Identify basic units and derived units
Recognise prefixes, multiples and submultiples of fundamental and derived units
Use scientific notation and significant figures in numerical problems
Demonstrate the use of various measuring instruments to determine length
Demonstrate the use of clocks and devices for measuring an interval of time
Identify factors that affect the period of a simple pendulum
Distinguish between mass and weight
Demonstrate how to measure mass and weight
Demonstrate how to locate the centre of mass of an object
Describe qualitatively the effect of the position of the centre of mass on the stability of an object
Determine the density of floating objects
Determine the density of a mixture of liquids
Describe what relative density is
Calculate relative density of air
Describe what scalar and vector quantities are
Distinguish between scalars and vectors
Demonstrate adding of vectors to determine a resultant
Demonstrate how to determine the resultant of two vectors graphically
Describe the terms used in mechanics
Demonstrate the use of equations of uniformly accelerated motion to solve problems
Interpret graphical representation of distance-time, displacement-time, speed-time, velocity-time and acceleration-time
Investigate the consequences of over speeding
Describe the acceleration of free fall for a body near the earth
Describe qualitatively the motion of bodies falling in a uniform gravitational field with and without air resistance
Explain what force is
Explain the effect of forces on bodies
Describe the inertia law
Demonstrate the relationship between force and acceleration
Demonstrate the relationship between mass and acceleration
Perform calculations on force
Investigate the effect of force on a spring
Demonstrate the effects of friction on the motion of a body
Describe the motion in a circular path due to a perpendicular force
Perform calculations based on the principle of moments
Investigate the everyday application of moments
Explain the meaning of the terms work, energy and power
Identify the units of measurement for work, energy and power
Calculate work using the appropriate formula
Identify the different forms of energy
Explain qualitatively and quantitatively the terms gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy
Describe sources of renewable and non-renewable energy
Explain the effects of the use of energy sources on the environment
Demonstrate energy transformation from one form to another
Describe the conservation of energy
Calculate energy using mass and velocity
Demonstrate the calculation of efficiency of energy conversion using the appropriate formula
Demonstrate calculation of power using the appropriate formula
Describe what a simple machine is
Identify the different types of simple machines
Describe the distances moved by the effort and the load in a simple machine
Explain the terms Mechanical Advantage (MA), Velocity Ratio (VR) and Efficiency
Perform calculations involving simple machines
Explain what pressure is
Describe how pressure relates to force and area using appropriate examples and formula
Identify factors affecting pressure in liquids
Describe the transmission of pressure in hydraulic systems
Calculate pressure in liquids
Explain the mechanism of a mercury barometer
Explain the mechanism of a manometer
Explain principles of upthrust and floatation
Describe how upthrust relates to floatation in fluids
